transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess it’s gotten kind of ridiculous with elevators. Like I’m starting to plan my whole day around avoiding them. I’ll take five flights of stairs at home instead, which sounds like good exercise, I know, but it’s not really about that.

And I actually turned down this workshop because it was in a high-rise, which is embarrassing because I’m supposed to be the training guy, you know? I work with people on computer stuff, and now I’ve even stopped visiting one of my older students because his building doesn’t really have another option besides the elevator. So… yeah, that’s why I’m here.
What is it about elevators that scares you most?

Mostly it’s the idea of getting stuck, I think. Or, like… dropped. I know that sounds dramatic, because obviously office elevators are running all day and people use them without thinking. I mean, I’ve been in plenty of buildings where nobody’s worried, they’re just checking their phones or whatever.

But when I’m standing there and I see those older doors, like in my apartment building or sometimes at work, my brain just kind of goes, nope, this thing is going to trap you in there. Or it’s going to fall. And part of me knows that’s probably not realistic, but it doesn’t really matter in the moment.
When you have to get into an elevator, do you get a sudden rush of intense fear or panic?

Yeah, pretty much right away. Like as soon as I’m walking toward one, or I hear that clunk when it opens, my chest tightens and my hands get sweaty, and there’s this rush of panic before I’ve even really thought anything through.

It’s weird because sometimes I’ll be fine a minute before, like thinking about work stuff or what I’m going to make for dinner, and then the doors open and it’s just… immediate.
Do you feel this same kind of fear in other situations besides elevators?

Not really in the same way, no. I mean, I can get nervous about other things, like anyone does, but elevators are the thing where my brain just goes straight to the worst-case scenario.

Like, I know an office elevator is probably safe—people are using it all day, maintenance signs, whatever—but then I see the older doors in my apartment building or at work, and it’s like my mind treats it as if I’m about to be trapped in there or dropped. Which, saying it out loud, sounds kind of over the top… but that’s what it feels like.
Do you feel that your fear of elevators is stronger than the actual danger?

Yeah, I think it is stronger than the actual danger. Like, I know if it’s an office building, people are using the elevator all day and it’s probably safe.

But then I’ll be looking at the old doors in my apartment building, or even at work, and my brain treats it like I’m about to get trapped in there or dropped. Which, I know, sounds kind of over the top when I say it out loud. It’s just hard to convince myself of that in the moment.
